biom-01-c3.text: David F. Williams (2019). Specifications for Innovative, Enabling Biomaterials Based on the Principles of Biocompatibility Mechanisms. Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology.
biom-01-c3.quote: the ability of a material to perform with an appropriate host response in a specific application.
biom-01-c3.claim: The 1987 Williams definition is the ability of a material to perform with an appropriate host response in a specific application.

biom-03-c3.text: Larry L. Hench, Julian R. Jones (2015). Bioactive Glasses: Frontiers and Challenges. Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology.
biom-03-c3.quote: Bioactive glasses were discovered in 1969 and provided for the first time an alternative to nearly inert implant materials.
biom-03-c3.claim: Larry Hench's 1969 discovery: a specific silicate glass composition (45S5 Bioglass: 45 SiO₂, 24.5 Na₂O, 24.5 CaO, 6 P₂O₅ wt%) bonds chemically to bone via a five-stage surface reaction.

biom-05-c2.text: M. D. Pierschbacher, E. Ruoslahti (1984). Cell attachment activity of fibronectin can be duplicated by small synthetic fragments of the molecule. Nature.
biom-05-c2.quote: The ability of fibronectin to bind cells can be accounted for by the tetrapeptide
biom-05-c2.claim: Erkki Ruoslahti's 1984 identification turned it into the most-used cell-adhesion peptide in biomaterials.

biom-08-c2.text: Stefan Wilhelm, Warren C. W. Chan et al (2016). Analysis of nanoparticle delivery to tumours. Nature Reviews Materials (reported by University of Toronto Engineering News).
biom-08-c2.quote: the median value was about 0.7 per cent of injected nanoparticles reaching their targets
biom-08-c2.claim: Chan's 2016 meta-analysis: median 0.7% of injected nanoparticle dose reaches tumors.
